name: Mangrove Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Western coast of costa rica (gulf of nicoya to golfo dulce)
description: This restricted species is found only along the Pacific coast of Costa Rica, most often in or near mangrove trees. Medium-sized hummingbird.

name: Long-tailed Glossy Starling
rangeDescription: Far southern mauritania to northern guinea eastward to southern sudan and northwestern south sudan
description: A large, extremely long-tailed, dark and glossy starling. Sometimes looks black, but in good light shows iridescence that is mostly blue-green, with a purple belly and tail.

name: Magnolia Warbler
rangeDescription: Eastern north america; winters to panama and west indies
description: Breeding males are striking and unmistakable: especially look for white wing patch, head pattern, and thick black streaks on underparts. Females and immatures are less obvious and might be mistaken for Canada Warbler, but combination of gray head, yellow underparts, white wingbars, and at least some dark streaks on the flanks is distinctive.

name: Baird's Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Siberia, northern alaska to greenland; winters in andes to southern south america
description: Long-winged, long-distance migrant similar to White-rumped Sandpiper but with warmer buffy-tan plumage. Elongated body gives a horizontal impression when foraging; unique flattened oval shape when seen head-on.

name: Rock Eagle-Owl
rangeDescription: Indian subcontinent to himalayan foothills and western myanmar
description: Large brown “horned owl” of rocky hills and semi-desert, as well as thorn scrub and groves in arid areas. Very similar in appearance to Eurasian Eagle-Owl, but note weaker streaking on the underparts and smaller size; range overlap is limited.

name: St. Vincent Amazon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of st. vincent (lesser antilles)
description: A stout inhabitant of wet montane forests where it is typically found near the canopy. Seen well, this species presents a unique rainbow of colors.

name: Alpine Munia
rangeDescription: Southwestern new guinea (wharton and owen stanley mountains)
description: A small, little-known bird of alpine grasslands of southeastern New Guinea. Adult has thick, silver bill, black face, brown back, yellow rump, whitish chest and sides, black from under the tail, along the sides of the pale belly, meeting at the lower chest.

name: Nahan's Partridge
rangeDescription: Northeastern democratic republic of the congo and western uganda
description: Unusual francolin that is small and very dark, with a thick tail that is usually cocked up. A good view reveals red legs, red bare skin around the eye, and bright white markings on the breast and neck.

name: Brown-headed Gull
rangeDescription: Mountains of south-central asia; winters to arabia, india, and southeastern asia
description: The pale button eyes of this gull give it a somewhat fearsome appearance. Breeding adult’s head is the color of milk chocolate, lightening towards the bill.

name: Vinaceous Dove
rangeDescription: Dry savanna of sub-saharan africa
description: A fairly plain, typical-looking dove that is the default dove in much of the Sahel of northern Africa. The head and breast are pinkish-gray, and the neck has a black mark.

name: Taveta Golden-Weaver
rangeDescription: Riverine scrub of far southeastern kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: Breeding male is rich yellow with darker orange patches on the breast and the rear part of the crown. The female is dark on the back and buffy yellowish below with a pale base to the bill.

name: Hispaniolan Mango
rangeDescription: Hispaniola and satellite islands île-á-vache, tortue, gonâve, and beata
description: Hispaniola’s largest hummingbird. Adult male has a glittering green throat, black underparts, and violet tail.

name: Venezuelan Flowerpiercer
rangeDescription: Mountains of northeastern venezuela (northwestern monagas and southern sucre)
description: Small tanager-like bird with sharply hooked, slightly upturned bill, male all black and female yellow-olive. Both sexes show a white flash under the wing, better visible in flight.

name: Ituri Batis
rangeDescription: Humid forest of democratic republic of the congo and adjacent western uganda
description: A very small and striking gray, white, and black flycatcher-like bird with a very dark crown, a yellow eye, white wingbars, and a white spot above the bill base. Sexes similar.

name: Orange-bellied Parrot
rangeDescription: Breeds southwestern tasmania; winters to coastal southeastern australia
description: Small grassy-green parrot that feeds on the ground. Bright green and yellow with blue wings and yellow lower belly with a central orange patch, yellowish throat, and thin mid-blue line between eyes.

name: Red-legged Kittiwake
rangeDescription: Komandorskiye, aleutian, and pribilof islands; winters north pacific
description: Crisp small gull with very limited range; breeds on rocky cliffs on islands in the Bering Sea, from Alaska to Russia; winters on open ocean. Size and plumage most similar to Black-legged Kittiwake, but back is darker gray, yellow bill is shorter, legs are shorter and bright red, and underwing is darker gray.

name: Manchurian Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Northern manchuria; winters to southern china and thailand
description: Small, shy, and poorly understood, this reed warbler breeds in the remote marshlands of northeastern China and Russia and winters in drier, grassier habitats in Southeast Asia. Warm brown overall with a clean-cut whitish brow and throat; brow extends well behind the eye, unlike in Blunt-winged Warbler.

name: St. Lucia Warbler
rangeDescription: St. lucia (lesser antilles)
description: This small brightly colored bird feeds actively within middle to upper levels of forests. The combination of blue-gray upperparts, extensively yellow underparts, white wingbars, and bold facial pattern are unique within its range.
imageCreditName: Stu Elsom - Stuart Elsom Ecology / Rockjumper Birding Tours

name: Buru White-eye
rangeDescription: Mainly montane forest of buru (southern moluccas)
description: A small songbird with a prominent white eye-ring, a narrow yellow band on the forehead, green upperparts, a yellow rump, and an entirely yellow underside. Small groups roam the upper levels of forest, scrub, and patches of trees on farmland in the lowlands and foothills.

name: Yellow-headed Manakin
rangeDescription: Western and central andes of colombia and northeastern ecuador
description: Rare and local in cloud forest from around 1,200-2,400m. Unique: mostly olive with contrasting yellow crown and dull reddish eye.
